newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African business says limited support for strike.
newsitem.headline: S.African business says limited support for strike.

text.p: Support for Monday's one-day national strike has proved limited with far fewer marchers turning out to protest against labour legislation than anticipated, the South African Chamber of Business (Sacob) said.

"The overall impression gained was that the call for a national stayaway did not receive the degree of support that Cosatu (Congress of South African Trade Unions) may have expected," Sacob said in a statement.
Sacob said many employers had made contingency plans to cope with the 24-hour action either by employing temporary replacement labour, closing down for the day or granting leave to workers.
This had minimised the impact on business of the action, which was called to protest at the planned Basic Conditions of Employment Bill.

The bill, approved by cabinet in April, sets a 45 hour working week and four months maternity leave. Cosatu, the biggest union federation with 1.9 million members, wants a 40 hour week, six months maternity leave and the minimum age for formal employment to be set at 18.
